import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Kaptos supports multiple account types to handle various authentication schemes on the Aptos network. This page covers how to create and manage:

- Legacy Ed25519 (`Ed25519Account` / `Account.generate()`)
- SingleKey (`SingleKeyAccount`) with unified auth
- MultiKey (`MultiKeyAccount`) for threshold signing
- SDK-managed accounts via `Aptos` factory methods
- Custom authentication schemes via [Account Abstraction](/build/sdks/community-sdks/kotlin-sdk/account-abstraction)

## Legacy Account (Ed25519)

The legacy account type represents an account using the Ed25519 authentication scheme.

```kotlin
val legacy = Account.generate()

val fromPrivateKey = Account.fromPrivateKey(Ed25519PrivateKey("0x..."))
```

## SingleKey Account (Ed25519 or Secp256k1)

The unified `SingleKeyAccount` supports either Ed25519 or Secp256k1 signing schemes.

```kotlin
val ed25519Single = SingleKeyAccount.generate(scheme = SigningSchemeInput.Ed25519)
val secp256k1Single = SingleKeyAccount.generate(scheme = SigningSchemeInput.Secp256k1)

val fromKey = SingleKeyAccount(
  privateKey = Ed25519PrivateKey("0x...")
)
```

## MultiKey Account (Threshold Signing)

A `MultiKeyAccount` allows you to require multiple signatures from a defined set of public keys (threshold signing) to authenticate transactions.

```kotlin
val signerA = SingleKeyAccount.generate(scheme = SigningSchemeInput.Ed25519)
val signerB = SingleKeyAccount.generate(scheme = SigningSchemeInput.Secp256k1)
val signerC = SingleKeyAccount.generate(scheme = SigningSchemeInput.Ed25519)

val multiKeyAccount = MultiKeyAccount.fromPublicKeysAndSigners(
  publicKeys = listOf(signerA.publicKey, signerB.publicKey, signerC.publicKey),
  signaturesRequired = 2,
  signers = listOf(signerA, signerC),
)
```

## SDK-Managed Accounts

When using the `Aptos` client, you can use factory methods that automatically manage the lifecycle of private keys, ensuring they are securely handled and closed automatically.

```kotlin
aptos(AptosConfig(network = Network.DEVNET)) {
  val alice = account()  // Ed25519 by default
  val bob = singleKeyAccount(SigningSchemeInput.Secp256k1)
  // Private keys are cleared automatically when this block exits
}
```

You can also instantiate accounts from parsed or unparsed AIP-80 formatted keys:

```kotlin
// From an AIP-80 string
val fromString = aptos.ed25519Account("ed25519-priv-0x...")

// From a parsed AIP-80 key
val fromParsed = aptos.account(Aip80PrivateKey.parse("ed25519-priv-0x..."))
```

### AIP-80 Private Key Format

AIP-80 defines a standard format for representing private keys as strings using a prefix (`ed25519-priv-`, `secp256k1-priv-`) followed by the hex-encoded key. This makes keys more portable across different languages and ecosystems while preserving their type.

## Account Discovery

You can discover accounts on-chain by their public key or derive owned accounts from a signer.

```kotlin
val accounts = aptos.accounts.findByPublicKey(publicKey)
val ownedAccounts = aptos.accounts.deriveOwned(signer)
```

## On-chain Account Creation

Generating an account locally only creates the credentials. To use the account on-chain, it must be created by funding it.

```kotlin
aptos.faucet.fund(alice.accountAddress, 100_000_000UL)
```

## Account Abstraction

For custom verification logic through Move modules or deriving Aptos accounts from external wallets (such as Solana wallets with Sign-In with Solana), refer to the [Account Abstraction guide](/build/sdks/community-sdks/kotlin-sdk/account-abstraction).
